documents.title: Medical Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
MEDICAL ONCOLOGY — FOLLOW-UP 1/15/2026
SCLC (limited stage), one year from diagnosis. CT chest/abdomen 1/12/2026: residual right hilar mass and hilar nodes unchanged from September; no new pulmonary, hepatic or adrenal lesions; pancreatic bed without mass. CA 19-9 normal. Sodium in the low 130s on salt tablets.
Plan: imaging every 4 months. Return in April.
Allergies: sulfa, shellfish.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy e-request: insulin glargine pens, pen needles, metformin 1000 mg. Seen 12/19, A1c 7.0. Approved 90-day supplies with 1 refill per PCP protocol.

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called to cancel 3/31 visit; has oncology and urology appointments in April and would rather not make three trips in a month. Asked to rebook after those. Message routed to PCP.

documents.title: Lower back
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My lower back has been aching for a few weeks and it's getting worse, especially at night. Tylenol takes the edge off. I see urology on the 27th anyway for my yearly bladder check and I'll tell them. Pants are loose again too. Do you want me to do anything before then?

documents.title: RE: Lower back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, Michael. With your history I'd like to look at you rather than wait; we have openings this week, call the front desk or reply here and we'll fit you in. If you'd rather keep it to the urology visit, please make sure they hear about the back pain and the weight. Go straight to the ED for any leg weakness or numbness, trouble controlling your bladder or bowels, or fever. Acetaminophen up to 650 mg every 6 hours is fine.

documents.title: RE: RE: Lower back
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I'll stick with urology on the 27th, they're doing a scan anyway. Legs are fine. I'll let you know.

documents.title: Urology Clinic Letter
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY — CLINIC LETTER
Visit 4/27/2026; addendum 5/14/2026.

He returns for urologic follow-up with a history of low-grade bladder cancer, CPFE, treated pancreatic adenocarcinoma and small cell lung cancer. Main concern is low back pain that has been worsening, along with further weight loss. Longstanding hesitancy and nocturia.

Problem list (as recorded): idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; pancreatic adenocarcinoma (mucin-producing) with chronic DIC; bladder cancer; hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis; suspected malignant neoplasm of lung; CPFE; COPD with emphysema; diabetes secondary to pancreatic insufficiency; BPH with LUTS; tobacco use disorder in remission.
Meds: metformin, insulin glargine, tiotropium, albuterol, tamsulosin, acetaminophen, nocturnal oxygen, pancrelipase, sodium chloride tablets.
Allergies: sulfa (rash), shellfish.
Family history: brother with prostate cancer at 68.

Exam: Digital rectal exam: prostate firm and nodular.
PSA 4/27/2026: 64 ng/mL.
Bone scan 5/4/2026: multiple foci of increased uptake in the lumbar spine and pelvis, consistent with metastases.
Transrectal prostate biopsy 5/11/2026: adenocarcinoma of the prostate, ISUP grade group 4.

Assessment: metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma to bone.
Plan: androgen deprivation with leuprolide 22.5 mg every 3 months, first injection 6/2/2026. Bicalutamide 50 mg daily starting 5/26/2026 for 4 weeks to cover the initial testosterone surge. Discussed with his oncologist. Continue tamsulosin.
cc: PCP, medical oncology

documents.title: PCP Call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called after reading urology's letter: new prostate cancer with spread to the bones of the low back and pelvis. He had already heard it from urology and has the hormone shot scheduled for June 2. Back pain manageable with acetaminophen. Offered a visit to go over everything; he wants to get through the first injection and see me after. Reminded him of ED precautions for leg weakness or bladder/bowel changes.

documents.title: Urology Treatment Note
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY — INJECTION VISIT 6/2/2026
Leuprolide acetate 22.5 mg given intramuscularly, left gluteal. Started bicalutamide 50 mg daily on 5/26, to complete 4 weeks. Next leuprolide in 3 months (early September). PSA and testosterone with that visit.
Allergies: sulfa, shellfish.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: E-request for tamsulosin 0.4 mg and tiotropium capsules. Last PCP visit 12/2025; follow-up booked September. Approved 90 days each. Left voicemail reminding pt of the 9/15 appointment.
